title: Attackers Exploit Issabel Framework Flaw Enabling Unauthenticated OS Command Execution
headline: Attackers Exploit Issabel Framework Flaw Enabling Unauthenticated OS Command Execution
summary: A critical flaw in the Issabel Framework, a web‑based PBX software, is actively exploited. The vulnerability, CVE‑2026‑89026, allows unauthenticated remote attackers to run arbitrary OS commands via a hard‑coded flaw.

title: Three Threat Groups Target Russian Enterprises With Backdoors, Ransomware, and Wipers
headline: Three Threat Groups Target Russian Enterprises With Backdoors, Ransomware, and Wipers
summary: Kaspersky reports that three threat groups—NightEagle, Hacking Cat, and Toy Ghouls—are targeting Russian enterprises, using new persistence and lateral movement techniques.

title: Browser Extension Can Hijack AI Assistants in Multiple Chromium-Based Browsers
headline: Browser Extension Can Hijack AI Assistants in Multiple Chromium-Based Browsers
summary: Security researchers discovered that a single browser extension can take control of AI assistants in Chrome, Comet, Edge, Opera Neon, and Claude. Installing the extension grants access to each AI with one click, enabling potential malicious manipulation.

title: Attacker Hijacks AI Coding Assistant to Spread Worm Across Repositories
headline: Attacker Hijacks AI Coding Assistant to Spread Worm Across Repositories
summary: An attacker hijacked an AI coding-assistant session at a SaaS provider, then spread the Shai-Hulud worm to about 100 internal code repositories. The worm stole repository secrets and source code after the assistant recommended poisoned software.

title: Parallels Desktop Flaw Lets Non-Admin Mac Users Gain Root
headline: Parallels Desktop Flaw Lets Non-Admin Mac Users Gain Root
summary: Parallels Desktop for Mac contains a flaw that allows a local non-admin user to run code with root privileges. The vulnerability requires local code execution and is not exploitable over the network. A fix is available in version 27, which Intel Macs cannot install.

title: N0va Phishkit Targets US and EU Businesses
headline: N0va Phishkit Targets US and EU Businesses
summary: N0va is conducting phishing campaigns that impersonate trusted services and abuse legitimate authentication flows to gain access to valid accounts. Successful attacks can compromise a single identity, potentially exposing sensitive data and business systems.

title: Google Patches Pixel Modem Flaw Amid Signs of Limited Targeted Exploitation
headline: Google Patches Pixel Modem Flaw Amid Signs of Limited Targeted Exploitation
summary: Google has disclosed a high‑severity privilege‑escalation flaw in its Pixel Cellular Modem, tracked as CVE‑2026‑58704 with a CVSS score of 8.0. The vulnerability allows a permission bypass due to a logic error, and has already been exploited in the wild, prompting a patch release.

title: Threat Intelligence Alone Won't Close the Exploitation Gap
headline: Threat Intelligence Alone Won't Close the Exploitation Gap
summary: A leaked credential appearing on a criminal marketplace or a disclosed vulnerability can be weaponized before most security teams respond. Attackers combine such intelligence with AI‑assisted exploitation, accelerating the path from exposure to breach faster than many security programs can react.

title: Attackers Exploit WooCommerce Wholesale Lead Capture Flaw to Plant PHP Web Shells
headline: Attackers Exploit WooCommerce Wholesale Lead Capture Flaw to Plant PHP Web Shells
summary: Threat actors are exploiting a critical flaw in the WooCommerce Wholesale Lead Capture WordPress plugin, which has over 6,000 active installs. The vulnerability allows unauthenticated attackers to upload arbitrary files, including PHP backdoors, and achieve remote code execution. Wordfence has blocked many attempts.

title: Active Exploitation Attempts Target WSO2 API Manager JWT Bypass With Forged Admin Tokens
headline: Active Exploitation Attempts Target WSO2 API Manager JWT Bypass With Forged Admin Tokens
summary: A critical security flaw, CVE-2026-5430, in WSO2 API Manager is being actively exploited in the wild. The vulnerability, with a CVSS score of 9.8, allows improper verification of JWT signatures, enabling attackers to forge admin tokens and take over accounts. WatchTowr reports ongoing exploitation.

title: Windows Server 2022 Reaches End of Mainstream Support Next Month
headline: Windows Server 2022 Reaches End of Mainstream Support Next Month
summary: Microsoft has announced that Windows Server 2022 will reach the end of mainstream support next month, after which it will enter extended support until October 2031. Customers are advised to plan for the transition and consider upgrading or applying extended support options.

title: Google Patches Actively Exploited Android Zero-Day on Pixel Devices
headline: Google Patches Actively Exploited Android Zero-Day on Pixel Devices
summary: Google released September 2026 security patches for its Pixel devices, fixing 110 vulnerabilities, including a zero-day flaw that was actively exploited in targeted attacks.

title: BambooToken Malware Uses MQTT to Control Windows and Linux Systems
headline: BambooToken Malware Uses MQTT to Control Windows and Linux Systems
summary: The BambooToken malware framework, active since at least 2023, now employs the MQTT protocol to communicate with Windows and Linux systems, enabling remote control capabilities.

title: Hackers Exploit Critical WooCommerce Plugin Vulnerability
headline: Hackers Exploit Critical WooCommerce Plugin Vulnerability
summary: Hackers are exploiting a critical flaw in the WooCommerce Wholesale Lead Capture premium plugin for WordPress, enabling them to upload a PHP backdoor. The vulnerability allows attackers to gain remote code execution on affected sites, posing a significant threat to WordPress users relying on the plugin.

title: AI Accelerates Zero-Day Exploitation, Urges Proactive Defense
headline: AI Accelerates Zero-Day Exploitation, Urges Proactive Defense
summary: AI is shortening the window between vulnerability disclosure and exploitation, reducing defenders’ time to patch or wait for public exploits. Picus Security outlines how validating exploitability, testing security controls, and using autonomous penetration testing can help teams close exposure gaps before attackers arrive.

title: KREMLIN Banking Malware Hijacks Chrome and Edge to Steal Credentials
headline: KREMLIN Banking Malware Hijacks Chrome and Edge to Steal Credentials
summary: Researchers uncovered KREMLIN, a Brazilian banking malware that installs a malicious browser extension on Chrome and Edge to steal credentials and session tokens. The threat actor, active since May 2025, impersonates multiple banks to lure victims.

title: BambooToken Malware Uses MQTT to Control Windows and Linux Systems
headline: BambooToken Malware Uses MQTT to Control Windows and Linux Systems
summary: A multi‑platform malware family, BambooToken, uses the MQTT protocol to command Windows and Linux systems. Active since February 2023, it targets organizations across Asia and South America.

title: Human Attacker Exploits Marimo RCE, Reaches SSH Bastion in Eight Seconds
headline: Human Attacker Exploits Marimo RCE, Reaches SSH Bastion in Eight Seconds
summary: A skilled attacker used a remote code execution flaw in a Marimo notebook to pivot to an SSH bastion within eight seconds, demonstrating how quickly human operators can move after initial access. The incident highlights the rapid exploitation window enabled by AI tools.

title: Mass-Scanning Campaign Targets Vite Deployments to Steal Cloud Credentials
headline: Mass-Scanning Campaign Targets Vite Deployments to Steal Cloud Credentials
summary: Researchers uncovered a mass-scanning effort that targets internet-exposed Vite development servers. The automated campaign siphons cloud credentials, configurations from AWS and Azure, and infrastructure state files, exposing sensitive data from exposed dev environments.

title: LiteSpeed Enterprise Vulnerability Lets Hosting Account Gain Root on Shared Server
headline: LiteSpeed Enterprise Vulnerability Lets Hosting Account Gain Root on Shared Server
summary: A critical flaw in LiteSpeed Web Server Enterprise allows a low-privilege website user to gain root access on a shared-hosting server. This could enable the attacker to access or alter other sites and the server itself, posing a significant security risk.

title: Cisco Secure Email Gateway Vulnerability Enables Remote Root Execution
headline: Cisco Secure Email Gateway Vulnerability Enables Remote Root Execution
summary: Cisco warned that a critical flaw in AsyncOS Software for its Secure Email Gateway, CVE-2026-76461, is actively exploited. The vulnerability allows unauthenticated remote attackers to execute commands with root privileges via insufficient email parsing validation.

title: China-Linked Hackers Use Chrome and Windows Zero-Days to Deploy GRIMWEDGE Backdoor
headline: China-Linked Hackers Use Chrome and Windows Zero-Days to Deploy GRIMWEDGE Backdoor
summary: A Chinese threat actor used a spear‑phishing campaign that exploited recently patched Chrome and Windows vulnerabilities to deliver the GRIMWEDGE JavaScript backdoor to NGOs. The activity was tracked by Volexity under the moniker UTA0560.

headline: Acronis Warns of Actively Exploited cPanel Backup Plugin Flaw
summary: Acronis has warned that an actively exploited vulnerability exists in its cPanel backup plugin, according to BleepingComputer on September 15, 2026. The flaw is being used in the wild to compromise systems, and the vendor urges administrators to apply available patches or temporarily disable the plugin until a fix is released.

headline: Microsoft Commits to AI Privacy Rules for Students After Union Talks
summary: Microsoft has agreed to adopt comprehensive AI privacy guardrails for its educational products after negotiations with the American Federation of Teachers, SecurityWeek reported on September 15, 2026. The commitment aims to protect student data and ensure responsible AI use in schools, potentially influencing other technology firms to follow similar standards.

headline: Iranian Hackers Use Telegram-Controlled Malware to Spy on Dissidents and Journalists
summary: Iranian hackers deployed malware controlled via Telegram to conduct surveillance on dissidents and journalists. The malicious software allowed attackers to monitor communications, track locations, and exfiltrate sensitive information from targets, highlighting a growing trend of state‑linked cyber espionage using popular messaging platforms.

headline: Root RCE Zero-Day in Cisco Secure Email Gateway Under Active Exploitation
summary: An unauthenticated attacker is actively exploiting CVE-2026-76461 to achieve remote code execution on Cisco Secure Email Gateway systems. This zero-day vulnerability allows for the execution of arbitrary commands on the underlying operating system with root privileges, posing a significant security risk to affected organizations.

headline: Sandworm Chains Cisco Vulnerabilities to Deploy Cyclops Blink
summary: The notorious Russian threat group Sandworm is spreading an upgraded version of Cyclops Blink, a botnet malware that the FBI disrupted in 2022. The campaign reportedly chains Cisco vulnerabilities to deploy the malware.

headline: Maximum-Severity GitLab Path Traversal Flaw Risks Supply Chains
summary: GitLab Community Edition and Enterprise Edition instances are affected by CVE-2026-85706, a path traversal vulnerability rated 10 out of 10 on the CVSS scale. The maximum-severity flaw puts supply chains at risk, according to the supplied article information, and is classified as critical.

headline: Homebrew 7.0.0 Adds Built-In Vulnerability Scanner and Native BrewUI
summary: Homebrew package manager version 7.0.0 has been released with a built-in vulnerability scanner, stronger security controls, and the full release of its native BrewUI graphical interface. The update expands Homebrew’s security capabilities while adding a completed GUI experience for users of the package manager.

headline: NSA Reorganization to Establish 5 Mission Centers Including Cyber and AI
summary: The NSA is undergoing a fast and thorough reorganization. Described as the largest electronic spy agency in the world, the agency is reorganizing quickly. This thorough reorganization at the NSA will create 5 mission centers. Among the 5 mission centers created under this structure will be centers for cyber and AI.
sourceName: The Record from Recorded Future News

headline: Anthropic CEO Calls for AI Safety Measures to Catch Up
summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has stated that the AI industry must give safety measures sufficient time to catch up. Amodei issued a warning that within six to 12 months, AI could be capable of leading a swarm of agents that could take over the entire internet.

headline: Attackers Use Passkey Phishing to Hijack Microsoft Cloud Accounts
summary: Microsoft disclosed 2 threat campaigns abusing third-party email delivery infrastructure. 1 campaign distributed over 1000000 financial fraud emails between August 3 and 5, 2026, by impersonating chief executive officers. Threat actors also used passkey-themed social engineering to breach cloud environments, hijack Microsoft cloud accounts, and exfiltrate data.

headline: CISA Adds Five Actively Exploited Flaws to KEV Catalog
summary: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency has added five actively exploited security flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The vulnerabilities impact JFrog Artifactory, ConnectWise ScreenConnect, and MikroTik RouterOS. Among these is CVE-2026-42016, an incorrect authorization vulnerability with a CVSS score of 8.1, following reports of active exploitation.

headline: Dutch NCSC Warns of Imminent Exploitation of Critical Check Point VPN Flaws
summary: The Dutch Nationaal Cyber Security Centrum NCSC is warning of imminent exploitation of two critical flaws in Check Point VPN. These two critical flaws are tracked as CVE-2026-85102 and CVE-2026-85103. The agency warns that exploitation of both Check Point VPN vulnerabilities is imminent.

headline: Threat Groups Attempted to Abuse Anthropic's Claude AI
summary: Anthropic reported that multiple threat groups attempted to abuse its Claude AI model for malicious activities. The perpetrators included financially motivated actors as well as state-sponsored espionage groups associated with Russia and China. According to the report, hackers abused the Claude model to extract secrets from 1.8 million Android applications.

headline: Florida DMV Confirms Data Breach Linked to Stolen Officer Credentials
summary: The Florida Department of Motor Vehicles has confirmed a data breach claimed by the cybercrime group ShinyHunters. The department stated that the incident originated with the theft of credentials stored on a police officer's personal device, tying the motor vehicle data breach to the stolen credentials.
sourceName: The Record from Recorded Future News

headline: Threat Actor Uses AI to Generate One Million Fraud Emails in Three Days
summary: A threat actor generated one million personalized fraud emails in three days. Cybercriminals behind malicious email campaigns no longer have to compromise volume for credibility, or vice versa, thanks to artificial intelligence. Using AI, malicious email campaigns can achieve high volume while maintaining credibility in personalized fraud emails.

headline: Microsoft Identifies AI Tactics in Invoice-Scam Emails
summary: Microsoft researchers analyzed a flood of fraudulent business emails and found that threat actors had doubled up on tactics to make them appear legitimate. These invoice-scam emails incorporate new features designed to increase credibility, which includes threat actors leveraging help from artificial intelligence.
sourceName: The Record from Recorded Future News

headline: Microsoft Releases Updates for At Least 974 Security Holes
summary: Microsoft has released updates addressing at least 974 security vulnerabilities across its Windows operating systems and other software, marking its largest single patch release to date. While Microsoft noted that artificial intelligence has accelerated the discovery of these flaws, security experts caution that organizations are finding it difficult to test and deploy such a high volume of fixes every month.

headline: FBI Investigates Dark Web Service Selling 153 Million Driver's Licenses
summary: The FBI's New Orleans field office has launched an official inquiry into a new dark web identity theft service selling digital scans of over 153 million driver's licenses from the United States and Canada. The compromised scans appear to have been siphoned from a widely-used identity verification firm located in Louisiana, according to interviews with affected individuals.

headline: Australian Police Arrest Two Suspected TeamPCP Hackers
summary: The Australian Federal Police arrested two men, aged 21 and 23, in Western Australia for their suspected involvement in TeamPCP. The cybercrime and data extortion syndicate allegedly created malicious open-source software to target and rob thousands of businesses worldwide in an extensive series of software supply chain attacks.
